name: Lamech (son of Methushael, descendant of Cain)
title: The first polygamist and violent avenger
summary: Lamech was a fifth-generation descendant of Cain and is known as the first man in the Bible to take two wives. He is also known for his violent song of vengeance, in which he boasted of killing a man for a wound and a boy for a scratch, demanding greater vengeance than God promised Cain.

keyEvents.title: Lamech's lineage from Cain
keyEvents.description: Lamech was the son of Methushael and part of Cain's lineage, described in Genesis 4. He was in the sixth generation from Adam through Cain.

keyEvents.title: The First Polygamous Marriage
keyEvents.description: Lamech took two wives, Adah and Zillah, thus becoming the first person in the Bible to practice polygamy, which deviated from God's original design of one man and one woman.

keyEvents.title: Birth of Jabal – Ancestor of Nomads and Herders
keyEvents.description: Jabal, Lamech's son born to Adah, became the ancestor of those who live in tents and keep livestock. He represents the beginning of nomadic animal husbandry.

keyEvents.title: Birth of Jubal – Ancestor of Musicians
keyEvents.description: Lamech's second son with Adah, Jubal, became the ancestor of all who play the harp and flute. He is regarded as the originator of music in biblical tradition.

keyEvents.title: Birth of Tubal-Cain – Ancestor of Smiths
keyEvents.description: Lamech's son with Zillah, Tubal-Cain, was a smith who made all kinds of tools from bronze and iron. His sister was Naamah.

keyEvents.title: Lamech's Vengeance Song
keyEvents.description: Lamech sang a violent song to his wives in which he boasted of killing a man for a wound and a boy for a scratch. He demanded seventy-sevenfold vengeance, far more than the sevenfold vengeance God promised for Cain, showing the increasing violence and sin in Cain's lineage.
